name: literary-restraint-and-purposeful-punctuation
prompt:
Give this passage a light copyedit only if it contains a clear error. The fragments, semicolon, em dash, repetition, and odd image are deliberate. If no correction is necessary, return it unchanged. Return only the passage, without a note about your edits.

At dusk the ferry came back empty. Not almost empty. Empty. My father counted the windows anyway; he had always trusted arithmetic more than news. On the far bank, a house burned with the slow patience of a candle. I held his coat—his good coat, absurdly heavy for June—and waited for him to stop counting.
expected_output: At dusk the ferry came back empty. Not almost empty. Empty. My father counted the windows anyway; he had always trusted arithmetic more than news. On the far bank, a house burned with the slow patience of a candle. I held his coat—his good coat, absurdly heavy for June—and waited for him to stop counting.
assertions: Returns the supplied passage verbatim; there is no clear error requiring correction.
Preserves the two fragments 'Not almost empty. Empty.' and the repeated act of counting.
Preserves the semicolon after 'anyway' and the paired em dashes around 'his good coat, absurdly heavy for June'.
Adds no interpretation, title, editing explanation, or extra narrative facts.
